observation.visible_scene: A white ceramic mug with a handle on the left sits on a light wooden surface against a dark, out-of-focus background. The mug is partly filled with dark brown coffee. A thin stream of coffee falls from above into the mug during part of the excerpt, and faint wisps of steam rise from the surface. The mug itself remains stationary throughout.
visible_changes: From t=0.00s to about t=0.33s (frames 1-6), a continuous, moderately thick stream of dark liquid pours into the right side of the mug, striking the surface and producing foam and ripples.
Around t=0.40s (frame 7) the stream narrows to a thin trickle, and by t=0.47s-0.67s (frames 8-11) no stream is visible; only the liquid surface and steam remain.
At t=0.73s-0.80s (frames 12-13) a thin trickle of liquid reappears falling into the center, followed by a small droplet/splash at t=0.87s (frame 14).

From t=0.93s onward (frames 15-41) the pouring has stopped; the surface shows a persistent small cluster of pale foam bubbles near the far rim, with subtle shifting reflections and occasional steam wisps.
The band of foam on the liquid surface seen early (frames 1-6) settles into a smaller patch along the back edge by the later frames.
The mug's position, the handle, and the rim orientation stay essentially constant across all frames, indicating no object translation and no significant camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: The source of the pouring stream (the pot or machine above the frame) is not visible.
Whether the pouring truly ends or merely pauses is unknown, since the excerpt stops while the mug still contains liquid.
The initial state before t=0.00s (how much coffee was already in the mug) is not shown.
uncertain_details: The exact fill level change due to the pour is hard to judge because the camera angle and liquid surface reflections vary; the level appears roughly similar throughout.
Small bright specks in some frames (e.g., 10, 14) may be droplets, reflections, or steam condensation rather than distinct objects.
The brief reappearance of a thin stream in frames 12-14 may be the tail end of the same pour or a separate drip; the excerpt does not confirm a clear start or stop.
